limitations: "Four participants (H1, H12, N5, N6) noted that the system’s node-based layout displayed dense information that increased their mental workload." (PDF p. 13)

"Participants found the LLM-generated suggestions based on collected papers can sometimes still be too broad (H6, H10), not entirely trustworthy (N7, H11), and over-reliant on the scope of the collected papers, placing the effort on the users to find a representative initial set of papers (N3, N7, H10)." (PDF p. 15)
"Our studies involved participants from specific research areas in HCI and NLP, limiting the generalizability of our system and findings." (PDF p. 18)

"However, while the current predefined structure is generalizable across multiple research domains and scenarios, some participants desired even more structures in the form of finer-grained facets or by defining their own customized facets (H10, N3)." (PDF p. 18)
"The short timeframe of the lab study limits our ability to assess the long-term impact of IdeaSynth on research outcomes." (PDF p. 18)

"While our longer field deployment uncovered additional strategies participants employed to enhance real-world idea development, assessing the long-term quality, impact, or success of ideas generated through system usage remains a challenge." (PDF p. 18)
"While IdeaSynth used basic tools like search and a recommendation system to expand the paper set, the process remained largely manual." (PDF p. 19)
"However, some participants felt the scope of recommended papers was too limited to their existing collection, making it harder to find additional relevant work." (PDF p. 19)
boundary_conditions: "Therefore, we scope this project on the early idea development process and take a user-centered perspective, focusing on how IdeaSynth affected researchers’ ideation process based on participants’ self-perception." (PDF p. 18)
"We note that the main focus of IdeaSynth is not on literature discovery or understanding." (PDF p. 15)
"To address these concerns, IdeaSynth does not aim to automate the ideation process or replace the human researcher." (PDF p. 18)

quotes: "These recordings were manually transcribed and tagged to differentiate between teacher and student turns at talk as well as topic domain to guide the LLM during response generation." (PDF p. 3)
"This design allows users to query the student agents and get responses that are authentic to student discursive behavior." (PDF p. 3)

rq3_entries.value: the preservice teacher chooses whom to address, produces the teacher talk, and attempts to build consensus around the science topic (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Users control a teacher avatar and can interact with individual students or the whole class through a text-based dialogue box." (PDF p. 3)
"The facilitator provided a brief tutorial and then guided the participants over the session as they practiced engaging AI-students with a science topic and building consensus around it." (PDF p. 3)

the participant must continue initiating and steering the classroom dialogue; the paper reports no reduction in that responsibility as competence grows (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "The facilitator provided a brief tutorial and then guided the participants over the session as they practiced engaging AI-students with a science topic and building consensus around it." (PDF p. 3)

rq3_entries.value: single_session (1) — (PDF p. 3)
quotes: "Each participant was scheduled for a 1-hour simulation session guided by a researcher facilitator." (PDF p. 3)

claim_entries.value: the paper concludes that preservice teachers practiced productive discourse and developed ambitious science-teaching talk moves (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "In this study, preservice teachers were able to practice eliciting academically productive discourse and develop their ambitious science teaching talk moves." (PDF p. 9)

claim_entries.value: learning
empirical
case_study — the authors identify the design as a case study of participant discourse (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "This study uses a case study design to explore the dialogic behaviors of preservice teachers and AI-powered student agents in interaction." (PDF p. 2)
"We used nonprobability sampling to recruit 15 preservice math and science teachers (all female) from a teacher education program at a university in the southern US." (PDF p. 3)

claim_entries.value: domain_students — participants were preservice teachers enrolled in teacher education (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "We used nonprobability sampling to recruit 15 preservice math and science teachers (all female) from a teacher education program at a university in the southern US." (PDF p. 3)

claim_entries.value: baseline_system — an external in-situ classroom discourse dataset served as the model comparator (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "We also include the in situ classroom discourse of highly trained teachers and human students to use as a model comparison." (PDF p. 2)

claim_entries.value: descriptive_only — the analyses report percentages, sequence support and confidence, and transition probabilities without inferential tests (PDF pp. 4-5).
quotes: "A descriptive analysis of talk moves as percentages of total talk from both datasets is shown in Figure 3." (PDF p. 4)

"The results of the analysis are shown in Tables 2, 3 and 4, along with support, a metric indicating the proportion of sequences that contain the specified pattern in the dataset, and confidence, a measure of reliability with values closer to 1 indicating a higher probability of the pattern tail appearing given the first talk move of the sequence." (PDF p. 5)

claim_entries.value: 1-hour simulation session — (PDF p. 3)
quotes: "Each participant was scheduled for a 1-hour simulation session guided by a researcher facilitator." (PDF p. 3)

claim_entries.value: no fully theorized explanations occurred, and simulated minilecture/question turns formed an unproductive cycle (PDF pp. 5, 7).
quotes: "Fully theorized science explanations did not occur in either dataset." (PDF p. 5)

"When using the minilecture (Tml) talk move in the simulated classroom, preservice teacher had a 41% probability of receiving a student question (Sqn), which in turn had a 39% probability of transitioning to another minilecture, creating a cycle of unproductive academic discourse." (PDF p. 7)

claim_entries.value: claim_exceeds_evidence
the observed dialogue supports productive within-session performance, but one session without a change or transfer measure does not establish development of teaching skill (PDF pp. 3, 9).
quotes: "Each participant was scheduled for a 1-hour simulation session guided by a researcher facilitator." (PDF p. 3)
"In this study, preservice teachers were able to practice eliciting academically productive discourse and develop their ambitious science teaching talk moves." (PDF p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: preservice science-teacher dialogue practice in virtual classroom simulation (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "This study used a classroom teaching simulator called EVETeach, which employs open-source 3D virtual world technology to render a middle school science classroom populated with six AI-powered student agents." (PDF p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: learning_or_skill_development — EVETeach is designed to support preservice-teacher learning (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "EVETeach was designed and developed as part of an ongoing research project aimed at supporting preservice teacher learning [14]." (PDF p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: novice_or_learner — the users are preservice teachers in a teacher-education program (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "We used nonprobability sampling to recruit 15 preservice math and science teachers (all female) from a teacher education program at a university in the southern US." (PDF p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: execution_or_skill_gap — the support provides practice enacting academically productive classroom dialogue (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "One of the essential purposes of science teacher training simulations is for science teachers to practice facilitating academically productive talk [16], therefore it is important for student-teacher interactions in the simulations to be as authentic as possible." (PDF p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measures recurring dialogue sequences and transitions (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "These analyses allowed us to discern the most common patterns of academically productive talk moves within both datasets and to understand the probability of transitioning from one talk move to another." (PDF p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the simulator bounds practice as teacher-to-individual or teacher-to-class dialogue (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Users control a teacher avatar and can interact with individual students or the whole class through a text-based dialogue box." (PDF p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — generated student responses follow the participant's queries (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "This design allows users to query the student agents and get responses that are authentic to student discursive behavior." (PDF p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_or_foundation_model — a customized fine-tuned GPT generates the student dialogue (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "The student agents are controlled through a cloud-based program powered by a fine-tuned and customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) [4]." (PDF p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the scaffold's meaning is produced by a GPT language model (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "After evaluating multiple large language models (LLMs) we decided that GPT-2, an open-source large language model by OpenAI, was most suitable for our purposes due to its susceptibility to training data and low hallucination rates compared to larger models [15, 26]." (PDF p. 3)

limitations: "This may be due to the text-based format of the simulation-based dialogue, where responses were not as immediate as would occur during spoken discourse." (PDF p. 8)
"Another possibility is that preservice teachers had a low sense of social presence, the feeling of being in the simulation with another [6], which could influence their behavior [13]." (PDF p. 8)
boundary_conditions: "We used nonprobability sampling to recruit 15 preservice math and science teachers (all female) from a teacher education program at a university in the southern US." (PDF p. 3)
"We specifically looked for teacher-initiated patterns, as this was the only dynamic possible in the simulated classroom." (PDF p. 4)
"This was expected, as the data were based on lesson stages where teachers were introducing and building consensus on topics." (PDF p. 5)
cards.notes: - The empirical comparator is an external in-situ classroom discourse corpus from two professionally trained teachers, not a control condition or baseline system. `comparison` was coded `baseline_system`, which loses the paper's model-comparison design.
cards.work_domain: preservice science-teacher dialogue practice in virtual classroom simulation
cards.claim: the paper concludes that preservice teachers practiced productive discourse and developed ambitious science-teaching talk moves
